## Service: goose (19)

### `start-two-h1` Two first-level headings

- **Page:** [steps/start/](https://mgifford.github.io/record-a-goose-sighting/steps/start/)
- **Component:** Start page headings and related-links section
- **Category:** structure
- **Classification:** best-practice
- **WCAG:** 1.3.1 (claimed)
- **ACT rules:** none
- **Locators:** xpath `(//h1)[2]` The second h1 is the related-links heading.; role heading "Information about Geese"
- **Preconditions:** none
- **Interaction:** none
- **Expected behaviour:** Each page exposes one top-level heading, and subsections use a heading level that reflects the page structure.
- **Actual behaviour:** The page contains two h1 elements; the second is the related-links heading.
- **User impact:** Screen reader and outline users find a duplicate top-level entry and cannot tell which heading describes the page itself.
- **Affected capabilities:** screen-reader; cognitive
- **Detection:** accessibility-tree-inspection; assisted-visual-review. The DOM is valid and every heading has text; judging whether two h1s make sense is contextual.
- **Manual test:** Open the headings list and compare the outline with the visible structure.
- **Review:** reproduced-automatically (automatedReproduction: verified, manualReproduction: not-run, assistiveTechnology: not-run, independentReview: not-run)
- **Review note:** Automated reproduction asserts the DOM or rendered condition. That is not an assistive-technology observation and it does not independently confirm the WCAG claim.
- **Comparison control:** none recorded
- **Evidence:** The page contains two h1 elements; the second is the related-links heading.; tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps two first-level headings
- **Sources:** [WCAG 2.2 technique H42: Using h1-h6 to identify headings](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H42)
- **Provenance:** imported from `docs/original-goose-issues.json`, `data/defect-annotations.json`
- **Not applicable:** `fixtureId`, `actRules`, `controlFixtureId`

### `start-dom-visual-order` Related links appear in a different order to the DOM

- **Page:** [steps/start/](https://mgifford.github.io/record-a-goose-sighting/steps/start/)
- **Component:** Related links list
- **Category:** focus-order
- **Classification:** usability-concern
- **WCAG:** 2.4.3 (claimed)
- **ACT rules:** none
- **Locators:** css `.custom-list` The related-links list itself; CSS order is 1, 3, 2 while DOM order is Wikipedia, More, RSPB.
- **Preconditions:** none
- **Interaction:** none
- **Expected behaviour:** Focus and reading order follow the visual order of the related links.
- **Actual behaviour:** CSS order values are 1, 3, 2 while the DOM and Tab order are Wikipedia, More, RSPB.
- **User impact:** Keyboard and magnification users move through links in an order that contradicts what they see, and can lose track of focus.
- **Affected capabilities:** keyboard-only; screen-magnification; screen-reader
- **Detection:** assisted-visual-review; manual-keyboard-evaluation. Tools read DOM order; they do not notice that the rendered order differs.
- **Manual test:** Tab through the related links and compare the focus order with the visual order.
- **Review:** reproduced-automatically (automatedReproduction: verified, manualReproduction: not-run, assistiveTechnology: not-run, independentReview: not-run)
- **Review note:** Automated reproduction asserts the DOM or rendered condition. That is not an assistive-technology observation and it does not independently confirm the WCAG claim.
- **Comparison control:** none recorded
- **Evidence:** CSS order values are 1, 3, 2 while the DOM and Tab order are Wikipedia, More, RSPB.; tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the related links in a different visual order to the DOM
- **Sources:** none
- **Provenance:** imported from `docs/original-goose-issues.json`, `data/defect-annotations.json`
- **Not applicable:** `fixtureId`, `actRules`, `controlFixtureId`

### `start-new-tab` External link opens a new tab without warning

- **Page:** [steps/start/](https://mgifford.github.io/record-a-goose-sighting/steps/start/)
- **Component:** Related links: external RSPB link
- **Category:** navigation
- **Classification:** best-practice
- **WCAG:** 3.2.5 (claimed)
- **ACT rules:** none
- **Locators:** css `a[target="_blank"]`; role link "Visit the RSPB website"
- **Preconditions:** none
- **Interaction:** none
- **Expected behaviour:** A link that opens a new tab tells the user in advance, in text or through an accessible description.
- **Actual behaviour:** The RSPB link has target=_blank and its accessible name gives no advance warning.
- **User impact:** People who use a screen reader or keyboard may not realise a new tab opened and cannot use Back to return.
- **Affected capabilities:** screen-reader; keyboard-only; cognitive
- **Detection:** heuristic-analysis; manual-keyboard-evaluation. Whether a new tab is expected depends on the link text and the user context.

- **Locators:** css `fieldset`; role group The fieldset is exposed as an unnamed group because it has no legend.

- **Page:** [paca/?role=invalid&shadow=closed](https://mgifford.github.io/record-a-goose-sighting/paca/?role=invalid&shadow=closed)
- **Fixture:** `paca-invalid-closed`
- **Component:** element with a role attribute
- **Category:** aria-validity
- **Classification:** exploratory
- **WCAG:** none
- **ACT rules:** 674b10 unknown
- **Locators:** document-scope The target lives in a closed shadow root. Ordinary DOM locators cannot resolve it; accessibility-tree access must be reported separately.
- **Preconditions:** none
- **Interaction:** none
- **Expected behaviour:** The target satisfies ACT rule 674b10: Role attribute has valid value.
- **Actual behaviour:** Exploratory. A closed shadow root is not automatically a WCAG failure, and engine visibility is unsupported here. No ACT outcome may be recorded. No ACT outcome is claimed.
- **User impact:** An invalid role is ignored by browsers, so the element exposes an unintended implicit role and assistive-technology users receive the wrong interaction model.

- **Detection:** dom-inspection; accessibility-tree-inspection. ACT rule outcome only. A WCAG mapping has not been reviewed for this fixture.
